version.description: The exact version of the package for which this lock was generated.

declaredDependencies.description:
The set of declared dependencies used when generating this lock. This field is used to determine if
someone has edited {@link Pkg.Decl#dependencies}, in which case, the lock should be regenerated.

resolvedDependencies.description:
The set of locked/resolved dependencies. This set will be placed into
{@link DependencyResolutionSpec#preResolvedVersions} during dependency resolution, ensuring these versions are
configured in the {@link Pkg.Store} or an error is thrown.

The version of the lock that lives in {@link Pkg.Category#PACKAGE_LOCK} (next to {@link FileExt#PKG}) is a writable
file that is only generated if:
- {@link Pkg.Decl#dependencies} changes
- the lock is deleted
- the lock has a conflict
- {@link Pkg.Store.WriteSpec#ignoreLock}s is set.
Only dependencies which are not sourced from {@link Pkg.Store.Java} and {@link Pkg.Store.Db} can be specified
in this version of the lock. An error will be thrown if someone writes an element that is sourced from
{@link Pkg.Store.Java} or {@link Pkg.Store.Db}.

The version of the lock that lives in {@link Pkg.Category#CACHE} is a read only file that is always generated
during dependency resolution. It includes a flattened list of all dependencies, including those sourced from
{@link Pkg.Store.Java} and {@link Pkg.Store.Db}. It is used similar to other {@link Pkg.Category#CACHE} files
to help drive the behavior of the type system.

title:
Describes a lock for a {@link Pkg} that influences dependency resolution during development.
The elements in {@link #resolvedDependencies} will be placed into
{@link DependencyResolutionSpec#preResolvedVersions} during dependency resolution, ensuring those versions are
configured in the {@link Pkg.Store} or an error is thrown.

By default, {@link Pkg.Store} will retry resolution if an error is thrown when using the lock. This is to make
utilization of a lock at worst equivalent to the resolution behavior prior to the introduction of the lock.
Setting {@link Pkg.Store.Config#doNotIgnoreLocksUponResolutionError} will change the default behavior, but is
only recommended to be used during CI or validation.

To ignore a lock when writing to the {@link Pkg.Store}, set {@link Pkg.Store.WriteSpec#ignoreLocks}. This will
re-resolve dependencies and re-generate the lock.
name: Pkg.Lock
